entries.meaning: A DDS is 1 to 16384 pixels a side; a PNG at most 2048x2048 (the game draws a PNG texture too, and leaves out a bigger one). Bigger textures also cost phone players memory.
entries.fix: Scale it down. 2x or 4x the original size already looks sharp.

entries.title: A picture smaller than, or not the shape of, the texture it replaces
where: the check tool (npx playac-mod check)

page: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.dds is 32x32, smaller than the original 64x64: the game stretches it over the original's place, so it looks blurrier than the game's own texture
textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.dds is 128x64, not the shape of the original 64x64: the game stretches it to the original's shape, so it looks squashed

entries.meaning: Not an error: the game installs the mod and draws the picture. The name says the original's size (tex1_64x64_...); the game always draws your picture in the original's place, so a smaller one looks blurry and one of another shape looks squashed.
entries.fix: Paint at the original size, or 2 or 4 times it in both directions (128x128 for a 64x64).

entries.title: The game could not read a PNG texture
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

game: texture is not a PNG the game reads, left out: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.png
PNG texture could not be read (image data is damaged), left out: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.png

entries.meaning: The game draws a .png texture by decoding it itself. This file is not a PNG, or is damaged, or uses a kind of PNG the game does not decode, so it is left out (the reason in brackets says why). The rest of the mod loads.
entries.fix: Export the picture again as a plain 8-bit RGBA or RGB PNG from your paint program, or save it as a .dds.

entries.title: Too many PNG pixels across your mods
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

game: PNG textures are over 96 MiB of pixels, this one left out: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.png
PNG textures are over 24 MiB of pixels on a phone, this one left out: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.png

entries.meaning: Every switched-on mod's PNG textures together may decode to at most 96 MiB of pixels (4 bytes a pixel), 24 MiB on a phone or low-memory device. PNGs past that, in load order, are left out; DDS textures do not count.
entries.fix: Make your PNGs smaller (2x the original size is already sharp), switch off another texture mod, or save the big textures as compressed .dds (BC7 or DXT5).

entries.title: The same texture as a PNG and a DDS
where: the check tool (npx playac-mod check)

page: textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.dds and textures/tex1_64x64_0123456789abcdef_14.png are the same texture: the game uses only one of them (the first it finds when it scans the folder, which you cannot choose), so the other is never drawn

entries.meaning: Not an error: the game installs the mod. A .png and a .dds with the same name are the same texture, and the game keeps whichever it finds first. You cannot choose which.
entries.fix: Keep one of the two files and delete the other.

entries.title: A picture in the wrong kind of file
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "notes.txt" holds a PNG picture. Pictures go in .png or .dds files.
"a.png" is named as .png but holds a DDS texture. Save it in the format its name says.
"photo.png" is a picture in a format mods can't carry. Save it as PNG or DDS.

entries.meaning: Every file is checked for what it really holds. A picture renamed to .txt, .json or .md would reach players as text, where no moderator looks, so it is refused; so is a .png that is really a DDS (or the other way round), and JPEG, GIF, WebP and other formats.
entries.fix: Save each picture as a real .dds (textures) or .png, with the extension that matches what it is.

entries.title: A PNG with animation or app data
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "art.png" holds a acTL chunk, which a picture in a mod may not carry (an animation frame or app data). Export it again as a plain PNG.
"art.png" holds more than 64 KiB of metadata. Export it again without metadata.

entries.meaning: A PNG in a mod is a plain picture: no animation frames (APNG), no data hidden in extra chunks, and only a little metadata. Hidden data would go unreviewed.
entries.fix: Export the picture again as a plain PNG, with "save metadata" (EXIF, XMP, comments, color profile) switched off.

entries.title: A texture format the game cannot load
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "textures/a.dds" is not a DDS file.
"textures/a.dds" is a DDS format the game can't load (DXT3). Save it as BC7, DXT1, DXT5 or uncompressed 32-bit RGBA.
"textures/a.dds" is cut short.
"art.png" is not a PNG we can read.

entries.meaning: A .dds must be BC7, DXT1 (BC1), DXT5 (BC3) or uncompressed 32-bit RGBA; a .png must be a normal PNG. Other formats (DXT3, 16-bit, 24-bit) and damaged files are refused. The game skips a texture it cannot read, so it would never show.
entries.fix: Export again as BC7 or DXT5 (or uncompressed RGBA 8888) with no mipmaps.

entries.title: The game is not in a scene yet
where: Settings, Mods, Developer (open the game with ?moddev=1)

site: The game is not in a scene yet. Start or load your town, then try again.

entries.meaning: The inspector records what the game draws, and nothing is drawn on the title screen.
entries.fix: Load your town first, then press Record textures.

entries.title: That texture is no longer kept
where: Settings, Mods, Developer (open the game with ?moddev=1)

site: That texture is no longer kept. It shows again once the game draws it.

entries.meaning: The inspector keeps up to 512 textures and 16 MB, dropping the one drawn longest ago, and Stop recording frees them all.
entries.fix: Walk back to where the texture is drawn (it is recorded again), then Copy name, PNG, Flash or Export it.

entries.title: The starter mod could not be exported
where: Settings, Mods, Developer (open the game with ?moddev=1)

site: Select at least one texture
The mod id must look like yourname.mod-name (lower case letters, digits and -)
ZIP support is not loaded in the game page. Reload and try again

entries.meaning: Export needs at least one ticked texture and an id like yourname.mod-name (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, one dot).
entries.fix: Tick the textures you want, type an id like "yourname.my-textures", and press Export again. If ZIP support is missing, reload the page.

entries.title: Developer mode needs the game page
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: no developer-mode mod is running in this session
site: Start the game first: developer mode loads a mod into the running game page.

entries.meaning: A folder or a dev server is read into the game page, which is not up yet.
entries.fix: Press Play and wait for the title screen (or your town), then choose the folder or Connect again.

entries.title: The folder fails playac-mod check
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: Not loaded: the folder fails playac-mod check: mod.json: "id" is missing
Not reloaded: the folder fails playac-mod check: shops.json: a price must be a whole number of Bells, 1 to 99999

entries.meaning: playac-mod dev checks the folder on every save and sends nothing while it fails. The game keeps the last good copy.
entries.fix: Fix what the message (and the terminal running playac-mod dev) names. The reload happens by itself once it passes.

entries.title: Restart the game to load this change
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)
the Mod log in Settings, Mods

page: mod.json changed: restart the game to load it
site: mod.json changed: restart the game to load it.
The script cannot reload: it was not in mod.json at boot. Restart the game.
Textures cannot reload: the mod had no textures folder at boot. Restart the game.

entries.meaning: Lines, the shop, the script and textures reload while you play. mod.json is read once, when the game starts, so a change to it (or a script or textures folder it did not have at the start) waits for a restart.
entries.fix: Choose Restart now in the Developer section. Save your town first.

entries.title: The folder could not be read
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: no files
"main.lua" is not file bytes
site: The folder could not be read: the folder has more than 2000 files
Stopped watching the folder: The requested file could not be read

entries.meaning: The browser would not read the folder (permission lost, the folder moved or was renamed), or it holds more than a mod may.
entries.fix: Choose the folder again. Pick the folder with mod.json in it, not a parent of it. Hidden files and node_modules are skipped; anything else in it counts.

entries.title: That is not a playac-mod dev address
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: Use the address playac-mod dev prints: http://localhost and a port.

entries.meaning: The page only talks to a dev server on your own computer: http on localhost or 127.0.0.1.
entries.fix: Paste the address `npx playac-mod dev` prints, for example http://127.0.0.1:2604.

entries.title: The dev server refused this site
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server refused this site: start it with --origin http://localhost:5174

entries.meaning: playac-mod dev only answers playaconline.com and a few local addresses, so another website cannot read your folder. This copy of the game is on another address.
entries.fix: Start it with --origin and the address of the game page, for example `npx playac-mod dev --origin http://localhost:5174`.

entries.title: The dev server speaks another version
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server speaks protocol 2; this game reads 1. Update one of them

entries.meaning: The CLI and the game changed how they talk, and these two are different versions.
entries.fix: Update the CLI (`npx playac-mod@latest dev`), or reload the game page to get the newest one.

entries.title: The dev server could not be reached
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: Failed to fetch
The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server answered 404 for /__playac/index (is it playac-mod dev?)

entries.meaning: Nothing answered at that address, or what answered is not playac-mod dev. Safari blocks a secure page from reaching http on your computer.
entries.fix: Run `npx playac-mod dev` in your mod folder and use the address it prints. Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or choose the folder instead.

entries.title: A change was not reloaded
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)
the Mod log in Settings, Mods

site: Not reloaded: the game refused it
Not loaded: the stored copy does not match its id

entries.meaning: Developer mode checks every save by the same rules as installing a ZIP. A file that breaks one is not loaded, and the game keeps running the last good copy.
entries.fix: Fix the file the message names and save again. When the message names a rule, that rule has its own entry on this page.

entries.title: Visits are off in developer mode
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused
Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: A mod is loaded in developer mode, so friend visits are off: no other town has that mod. Unload it in Settings, Mods, then restart the game.

entries.meaning: A mod loaded from a folder is not installed and no one else has it, so your town would not match any other. Visits refuse it either way.
entries.fix: Unload it in Settings, Mods, Developer, then restart the game.

entries.title: Sharing is off in developer mode
where: Share a mod, when you upload

site: Sharing is off while a mod is loaded in developer mode. Pack the folder into a ZIP (playac-mod pack) and upload that, so what is reviewed is exactly what players get.

entries.meaning: What you share must be the exact ZIP players will get, not a folder still changing.
entries.fix: Run `npx playac-mod pack`, unload the developer copy, restart, and upload the ZIP.

entries.title: A texture file was left out
where: the Mod log in Settings, Mods
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

game: texture textures/grass.jpg not read: only .dds and .png files in the textures folder are textures
texture textures/grass.dds not read: the name is not a texture name (tex1_WxH_hash[_palette]_fmt.dds or .png)
texture textures/tex1_32x32_626709d910129694_193ca5974976e36e_8.dds could not be read: not a DDS this browser can draw (BC7, BC1, BC3 or RGBA)

entries.meaning: The game reads only files named the way the HD pack names them (tex1_WxH_hash..._fmt), as DDS or PNG, from the textures folder. Anything else there is skipped.
entries.fix: Name the file after the texture it replaces (the texture inspector copies the name for you), save it as .dds (BC7, BC1, BC3 or uncompressed RGBA) or .png, and reload.

entries.title: Your browser cleared your mods
where: the Mods tab

site: Your browser cleared your mods. Browsers can delete a site's stored data, for example when the device is low on space or the site has not been visited for a while. Install them again below.

entries.meaning: Installed mods live in the browser's site storage, and the browser deleted it (low space, or Safari after 7 days without a visit). The game asks the browser to keep mods, but a browser can still clear them.
entries.fix: Install the mods again (Browse mods, or your ZIPs). Keep your own mod ZIPs somewhere safe.

entries.title: The game stopped responding with mods on
where: the Mods tab

site: The game stopped responding the last time it started with this mod on: Tea House. It started without mods this time. Your mods are still installed.

entries.meaning: The game did not finish starting, or froze early, the last time it ran with these mods switched on, so it started once without any mods. Nothing was removed.
entries.fix: Players: turn the named mod off (or one of them at a time), then restart. Makers: test the mod alone; the usual causes are textures too big for the device (phones have 24 MB for all mods) or a script doing heavy work at start.

entries.title: Your mods could not be read
where: the Mods tab

site: Your mods could not be read: The operation is insecure.

entries.meaning: The browser would not open its site storage, where mods are kept. Private windows and blocked site data do this.
entries.fix: Use a normal (not private) window and allow site data for playaconline.com, then reload.

entries.title: The mods database could not be used
where: the Mods tab
Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: the mods database is held open by another tab
the developer mods database is held open by another tab
the mods database refused the change

entries.meaning: The browser's mod storage turned the change down: another tab of the game is updating it (a newer version of the page is moving your mods to a new layout), or the browser stopped the write (storage full, or site data blocked).
entries.fix: Close the game's other tabs, reload, and try again. If it keeps happening, free some space on the device or allow site data for playaconline.com.

entries.title: That mod is not installed
where: the Mods tab

page: that mod is not installed

entries.meaning: The Mods tab changed a mod that is no longer installed: another tab removed it meanwhile.
entries.fix: Reload the Mods tab to see your mods as they are now.

entries.title: Too many mods for one export
where: the Mods tab

page: Your mods are 600 MB together, more than the 512 MB one export can hold. Remove the mods you do not use, then export again

entries.meaning: "Export my mods" makes one ZIP in the browser's memory, and your installed mods together are more than it can safely hold.
entries.fix: Remove the mods you do not use and export again. Each mod is also its own ZIP you can keep from Browse mods or its author.

entries.title: Not enough room in the browser
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP

page: There is not enough room in this browser's storage for this mod: it needs about 40 MB and about 12 MB is free. Remove a mod you do not use or free some space on this device, then try again

entries.meaning: Mods are kept in the browser's site storage, and it is full or blocked (a private window, or site data switched off).
entries.fix: Remove a mod you do not use, free space on the device, or allow site data for playaconline.com. Private windows have very little room.

entries.title: More than 32 mods on
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: only the first 32 mods load
You already have 32 mods on, the most the game loads. Turn one off first

entries.meaning: The game loads at most 32 switched-on mods.
entries.fix: Switch off a mod you can do without, then restart.

entries.title: Over the room the game keeps for mods
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: This mod unpacks to 30 MB, more than the 24 MB the game keeps for mods on a phone, so it cannot be switched on here
the mods before it already fill the 96 MB the game keeps for mods

entries.meaning: All switched-on mods together can unpack to at most 96 MB, or 24 MB on a phone or a low-memory device. A new mod that does not fit is installed switched off.
entries.fix: Switch off a big mod, or as a maker, keep texture mods small (compressed DDS, only the textures you changed) so phone players can use them.

entries.title: Removed by the moderators
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart
Mods tab, when you install a ZIP

page: Removed by the moderators: holds art from another game. It cannot be switched on

entries.meaning: The moderators took this version down (the reason follows). Every copy, even one installed from a ZIP, is switched off at the next start and cannot be switched on.
entries.fix: Players: remove it, or install a newer version once the maker fixes it. Makers: read the review reason, fix the problem and upload a new version; players who update get it switched back on.

entries.title: The mod could not be unpacked at start
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: could not be unpacked (ENOSPC)
the stored mod does not match its id
the mod list could not be written

entries.meaning: The game could not unpack this mod from browser storage when it started, usually because the browser is out of memory or storage, or the stored copy was damaged.
entries.fix: Restart the game. If it stays, remove the mod and install it again.

entries.title: Script took too long
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: script took too long (over 200000 instructions)
script took too long (over 33 ms)
script took too long (over 100 ms)

entries.meaning: One event gets a budget of 200,000 Lua instructions per mod, and one event run is stopped past 33 ms of wall time. The main chunk, when the game starts, gets 100 ms. String patterns, table.sort/concat and memory use count too. Over it, the script is stopped for the rest of the session, so it can never freeze the game.
entries.fix: Do less per event: no long loops, cache results in local variables or the store, avoid patterns like ".-.-.-" on long text. pcall does not get around the budget.

bad.text:
on("day_start", function()
  local n = 0
  for i = 1, 1e9 do n = n + i end
end)

entries.title: Script kept the game waiting
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: script kept the game waiting (3 runs over 8 ms)

entries.meaning: All mods together get 4 ms of Lua time a frame. An event run over 8 ms is a strike, and three strikes stop the script for the session, even if each run stayed inside its instruction budget, so a slow script cannot make the game stutter.
entries.fix: Do less per event: keep work small and spread it over events, cache results in locals or the store, and avoid long loops or patterns on long text.

entries.title: Script ran out of memory
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: out of memory (4 MB per mod, 16 MB for all mods together)

entries.meaning: A mod's script can use 4 MB, and all mods together 16 MB.
entries.fix: Keep fewer and smaller tables; do not build big strings in a loop (collect parts and table.concat them once).

entries.title: on() with an event not in "hooks"
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: on(): 'talk' is not in this mod's "hooks" list in mod.json
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: on(): unknown event 'tick'

entries.meaning: A script can only listen to the events mod.json lists in "scripts.hooks", and only to real events (at api 1: talk, day_start, item_picked, enter_scene; from api 2 also migrate, hour_change, shop_buy, item_sold, fish_caught, bug_caught, letter_read, villager_moved_in, visitor_arrived, command_result, answer).
entries.fix: Add the event to "hooks" in mod.json, or fix its spelling in on().

entries.title: on() called from inside a handler
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: on(): handlers can only be added while the script loads, not from inside a handler

entries.meaning: Handlers are added once, while main.lua first runs. A handler cannot add more handlers, and neither can a function another mod calls with remote.call.
entries.fix: Call on() at the top level of main.lua, and keep a flag in a variable to switch behaviour later.

entries.title: More than 16 handlers for one event
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:20: on(): at most 16 handlers for 'talk'

entries.meaning: A mod can add at most 16 handlers per event.
entries.fix: Use one handler that does several things.

entries.title: store.set before a town is loaded
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: no town is loaded yet (the script's main part runs before the save loads): save from an event, or use store.client

entries.meaning: "store" is kept per town, and the main part of a script runs before the town loads, so store.set is refused there (store.get answers nil). This is an api 2 rule: a mod whose mod.json says api 1 keeps the per-browser store of level 1, usable in the main part.
entries.fix: Save from an event (day_start, talk, ...), or use store.client for data that belongs to the browser rather than the town.

entries.title: remote.add of a name "exports" does not list
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-lib/main.lua:3: remote.add: count is not in mod.json "exports" (a library offers what it lists)

entries.meaning: Your mod.json has "exports", so remote.add offers only the names it lists: the mods that use your library were promised exactly those.
entries.fix: Add the name to "exports" with a one-line description, or offer one that is listed.

entries.title: remote.add or remote.call refused
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: remote.call: tea.lib offers no function brew
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: remote.call: tea.lib is already running (a call back into it would be a cycle), refused
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: remote.add: functions can only be offered while the script loads
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:6: remote.call: tea.lib has not updated this town's data yet (its migrate runs after this one), refused

entries.meaning: remote.add offers a function while the script loads (names a-z 0-9 _, at most 32). remote.call copies nil, booleans, numbers, strings and tables of them (64 KB, 16 levels) to a running mod that offers the function; a call back into a mod already running is refused. Inside a migrate handler, a call into a mod whose own migrate has not run in that town yet is refused too: its data is still at the old version.
entries.fix: Check the mod is installed, on and offers that name (remote.has), pass plain data, and do not call back into the caller. In migrate, only change your own data; ask other mods in a later event, when every migration is done.

entries.title: store.set refused a value
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: only strings, numbers and booleans can be saved
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: the store would be over 8192 bytes, nothing was saved
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: key longer than 64 bytes

entries.meaning: The store keeps strings, numbers and booleans (not tables or functions), keys up to 64 bytes, values up to 1024 bytes, 8 KB per mod per town (and 8 KB in store.client, per browser), no zero bytes, no NaN. A refused set changes nothing, and the error stops the script unless you pcall it.
entries.fix: Save plain values, keep keys short, and turn a table into a string yourself if you must (for example "3,7,12").

entries.title: Something scripts may not do
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:2: setmetatable: __gc is not allowed in mod scripts (finalizers cannot be stopped)
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:5: tables with a __len metamethod are not supported here in mod scripts

entries.meaning: Some Lua features are switched off because they could run outside the time budget: __gc finalizers, and __len metamethods passed to table functions. io, os, load, require, dofile and debug do not exist at all.
entries.fix: Remove the metamethod. Use plain tables.

entries.title: The script's Lua state failed
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: the script's Lua state failed and was dropped
the script raised an error that is not a string

entries.meaning: The Lua engine for this mod failed in a way it cannot recover from, or the script raised an error with error({...}) instead of a string.
entries.fix: Raise errors with error("text"). If it says the state failed, report it with the mod: it is a bug in the game.

entries.title: A Lua syntax error
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row
the check tool (npx playac-mod check)

page: main.lua:4: unfinished string near '"hello'
main.lua:7: ')' expected near 'log'
game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:5: 'end' expected (to close 'function' at line 2) near <eof>
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: unexpected symbol near '='

entries.meaning: The script is not valid Lua 5.4, so it never starts: none of its handlers run, and the Mods tab says "Script stopped" with the file, the line and what Lua expected there. The rest of the mod (textures, lines, shop) still works. `npx playac-mod check` finds the same error before you install, when a Lua 5.4 `luac` is on your PATH (it says so when there is none).
entries.fix: Open the file at the line shown. Usual causes: a missing `end` (every function, if, for and while needs one), a missing `then` or `do`, a string with no closing quote, `!=` where Lua writes `~=`, or a `+` where Lua joins strings with `..`. The line Lua names is where it noticed, often just after the real mistake.

entries.title: The script raised an error
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:7: attempt to index a nil value (global 'io')
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: attempt to call a nil value (global 'give_item')

entries.meaning: A Lua error in your script: the text says which file and line. The script is stopped for the rest of the session; the rest of the mod (textures, lines, shop) keeps working. Common causes: a typo in a name, calling something that does not exist in the API (io, os, require, a function from a newer game), or indexing nil.
entries.fix: Open the file at the line number shown, fix it, reinstall and restart. Use log() to print values while you work, and pcall around code that may fail.

entries.title: A command not in "permissions"
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: give_item is not in this mod's "permissions" in mod.json

entries.meaning: A script may only use the commands its mod.json "permissions" lists, and only at "api": 2. Players see that list on the Mods tab.
entries.fix: Add the command to "permissions" (and say "api": 2), or stop calling it.

entries.title: Too many commands
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: set_flag: at most 4 commands in one event
send_letter: at most 3 a day for each mod
show_line: this mod already has 8 commands waiting
ask: the game's command queue is full (32), try later

entries.meaning: A mod may queue at most 4 commands in one event and, each game day, 3 letters, 5 items, 100 flags, 20 lines and 10 questions (counted when queued, kept across a reload). At most 8 of its commands wait at once, 32 for all mods.
entries.fix: Queue fewer commands: remember in the store what you already sent today.

entries.title: An item a command cannot hand out
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: give_item: item 0x2100 is money
send_letter: item 0xF000 is not an item or furniture the game has
give_item: a mod can only give its own new items, by "<this mod's id>:<item id>"
give_item: no item by that id in this mod's items file

entries.meaning: Items follow the shop's rules: no money, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils or reserved numbers. An item is a number, "0x" and four hex digits, or one of this mod's own new items by its full id.
entries.fix: Pick another item, or write it as "0x2800" or "yourname.my-mod:thing".

entries.title: A command's arguments are wrong
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: send_letter: text must be 1 to 192 characters
send_letter: the text does not fit a letter (6 lines)
ask: choices must be a list of 2 to 4 answers
set_flag: the key must be 1 to 32 of a-z 0-9 _ . -
show_line: text must be 1 to 400 bytes

entries.meaning: The command was called with something it cannot use. The limits: a letter 1 to 192 characters in 6 lines, from up to 8, paper 0 to 63; a line up to 400 bytes; a question up to 120 characters with 2 to 4 answers of up to 16; a flag key of a-z 0-9 _ . - up to 32, its text up to 64 bytes.
entries.fix: Check the call against the reference (/modding/reference/) and shorten the text.

entries.title: Commands are off in The City
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: commands are switched off in The City
send_letter: commands are switched off in The City

entries.meaning: In The City every command is refused: other players there do not have your mod, and nothing a mod gives may enter the shared town. Called in The City, a command returns nil and this reason; queued at home and applied after the player went there, it comes back as a refused command_result. Either way it does not count against the daily caps.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Try again at home (for example from enter_scene).

entries.title: Only the town's owner changes a town
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: only the town owner's game can change the town (you are visiting)
give_item: only the town owner's game can change the town (you are visiting)

entries.meaning: Visiting a friend, send_letter and give_item are refused (nil and this reason when called, or a refused command_result if the player left home after queueing) and do not count against the daily caps: only the town owner's game changes a town. set_flag, show_line and ask still work.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Send it once the player is home.

entries.title: A lent mod acts only in its town
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: a friend's mod lent for a visit acts only in their town

entries.meaning: A visitor whose game borrowed the host's mods for a visit restarts on them at home before the trip and again after it. There every command of a lent mod comes back refused, and its shop, Nook goods, board notices, items and renames do nothing: a lent mod never changes the visitor's own town or save. In the host's town it runs as a visitor's mod does.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Your mod runs normally for players who installed it.

entries.title: No room for a letter or an item
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: the mailbox and the post office are both full
the pockets, the mailbox and the post office are all full
the pockets are full (a new item cannot come by mail)

entries.meaning: The mailbox and the post office had no room, or the pockets were full for one of the mod's own new items (a letter cannot carry its identity).
entries.fix: Try again later; watch command_result and resend when it failed.

entries.title: A line or a gift could not be done
where: the command_result event (its error) and the mod log, when a command is refused

game: the text cannot be drawn in the window (too many pages?)
the item is not this town's to give (its mod is off, or this is not your town)
the flag could not be saved

entries.meaning: The game could not carry the command out: a line too long to page, a new item whose mod is off, or a flag the store refused (it would take the store over 8 KB).
entries.fix: Shorten the line, keep the mod on, or keep the store small.

entries.title: The name has a word the site does not allow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The mod's name has a word the site does not allow. Pick another name.

entries.meaning: The list of shared mods is public, so a mod's name goes through the same word filter as everything else players can read on the site.
entries.fix: Change "name" in mod.json, raise the version, and upload again.

entries.title: An author name has a word the site does not allow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: An author name has a word the site does not allow. Use another name.

entries.meaning: Author names are shown on the public list of shared mods, so they go through the site's word filter.
entries.fix: Change the name in "authors" in mod.json, raise the version, and upload again.

entries.title: Sign in to share
where: Share a mod, when you upload

site: Sign in to share a mod.

entries.meaning: Sharing a mod needs an account.
entries.fix: Sign in, then upload again.

entries.title: Accept the mod rules first
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Confirm your age and accept the mod rules before you share a mod.

entries.meaning: The first time you share, you answer your age and accept the mod rules.
entries.fix: Answer the questions above the upload button, then upload again.

entries.title: Sharing is for players 13 or older
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Sharing mods is for players 13 or older.

entries.meaning: Players under 13 can make and install mods but cannot share them.
entries.fix: Keep the mod for yourself, or ask a parent or guardian to share it from their own account.

entries.title: This account cannot share mods
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Mod uploads are switched off for your account.

entries.meaning: Mods from this account were removed for copyright several times (the repeat-infringer policy), or a moderator switched uploads off for it.
entries.fix: See the mod rules page for how to appeal.

entries.title: This version is already uploaded
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: This version of the mod is already uploaded. Raise the version in mod.json.

entries.meaning: Every upload is a new version and a version can never be replaced, so players who have it always have the same files.
entries.fix: Raise "version" in mod.json (1.0.0 to 1.0.1) and upload again.

entries.title: A screenshot is needed, or one could not be read
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Add at least one screenshot of the mod in the game (PNG or JPEG). It is shown on the mod's page.
Screenshot 1 must be a PNG or a JPEG.
Screenshot 1 must be 200 to 4096 pixels a side.
Screenshot 1 could not be read: is it a whole PNG or JPEG?
Each screenshot must be at most 2 MiB.
Send at most 4 screenshots.

entries.meaning: Every shared version needs 1 to 4 screenshots of the mod in the game, shown on its page: PNG or JPEG, 200 to 4096 pixels a side, at most 2 MB each. The server re-saves them, so no hidden photo data survives.
entries.fix: Add a screenshot in Share a mod, with playac-mod publish --shot, or in .playac/screenshots/ (also for a GitHub import).

entries.title: A changelog line is needed
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Say in one line what this version changes.
The changelog line must be 1 to 300 characters of text, with at most 4 line breaks.
The changelog line has a word the site does not allow. Say it another way.
Send one changelog line.

entries.meaning: Every shared version needs one line about what it changes, shown in its page's version list: up to 300 characters and 4 line breaks, and the same words filter as a mod's name.
entries.fix: Write the line in Share a mod, with playac-mod publish --changelog, or as this version's section of CHANGELOG.md.

entries.title: The upload form could not be read
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The upload form has no zip.
The upload form could not be read.
The upload form has a part this site does not read.
The upload form has no boundary.
Send one zip at a time.

entries.meaning: An upload is a form with the zip, the screenshots and the changelog line. This one was not sent the way the site sends it.
entries.fix: Share from Settings, Mods, or with playac-mod publish. A script of your own must send multipart/form-data with the parts zip, screenshot and changelog.

entries.title: Another player owns this id
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Another player already uploaded a mod with this id. Pick a different id.

entries.meaning: A mod id belongs to the account that first shared it.
entries.fix: Change "id" in mod.json, with your own name before the dot.

entries.title: Too many uploads
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: You can upload 5 mods an hour. Try again later.
You have 10 uploads waiting for review. Upload more once some are reviewed.

entries.meaning: There is a limit on uploads per hour and on uploads waiting for review at once.
entries.fix: Wait for a review, or try again in an hour. Test locally first so each upload counts.

entries.title: Your shared mods use all your space
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Your mods would take more than 64 MiB. Ask for an old version to be taken down, or make this one smaller.

entries.meaning: Each account has a total size for all its shared versions.
entries.fix: Ask for an old version to be removed, or make the mod smaller.

entries.title: Upload busy or too slow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Another upload from your account or your network is still going, or the server is busy. Try again in a minute.
Your connection was too slow to upload the zip. Try again on a better connection.

entries.meaning: One upload at a time per account and network, and the file has to keep arriving.
entries.fix: Wait a minute and try again, on a steadier connection if it was too slow.

entries.title: The images could not be checked
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: We couldn't check the images in your mod just now. Nothing was uploaded. Try again in a few minutes.

entries.meaning: Every image is checked before an upload is accepted, and the checking service did not answer. Nothing was uploaded.
entries.fix: Try again in a few minutes.

entries.title: The upload was refused
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: This upload can't be accepted.

entries.meaning: The upload was refused without a reason being given, or the account cannot share right now.
entries.fix: Read the mod rules. If you think it is a mistake, contact the moderators.

entries.title: Sharing mods is not open
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Sharing mods is not open yet. Mods you install from a ZIP file still work.

entries.meaning: The site has not opened mod sharing (or has closed it for now). Uploads and GitHub imports are both refused. Installing a mod from a ZIP file is not affected.
entries.fix: Keep making and testing the mod locally, and share it once sharing opens.

entries.title: Uploads are paused while reviews catch up
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: New mod uploads are paused while the review queue catches up. Nothing was uploaded. Try again in a few days.

entries.meaning: When the oldest upload has waited more than a week for review, new uploads and imports stop until the queue is shorter. Nothing was uploaded.
entries.fix: Try again in a few days.

entries.title: Two-factor sign-in is needed
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Turn on two-factor sign-in on your Profile page before you share a mod.
Enter the code from your authenticator app to share a mod.
Enter the code from your authenticator app to approve playac-mod.
Sharing mods is switched off on this server for now.

entries.meaning: Sharing a mod, importing one from GitHub and approving a playac-mod sign-in all need two-factor sign-in on the account, and a code entered in the last few minutes on this browser. If the server cannot check codes at all, sharing is switched off.
entries.fix: Turn on two-factor sign-in on your Profile page, then enter a code from your authenticator app when asked.

entries.title: The name before the dot is another player's
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The part of the id before the dot belongs to another player's account. Use your own name before the dot.

entries.meaning: The part of a mod id before the dot (kim in kim.tea-house) belongs to the account that first had a mod approved under it, so nobody else can publish under that name.
entries.fix: Change "id" in mod.json to start with your own name.

entries.title: These files were taken down
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: These files were taken down from the registry, so they can't be shared again.

entries.meaning: The same files as a version a moderator removed. Copies of it are switched off, and the files cannot be shared again under any id or version.
entries.fix: Read the review decision on the removed version and change what it named. If you think the removal was wrong, see the mod rules page.

entries.title: Too many upload attempts
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: You can try 12 uploads an hour. Try again later.

entries.meaning: Every upload attempt counts, refused ones too: each one costs a check of every image.
entries.fix: Check the mod locally first (npx playac-mod check), then try again in an hour.

entries.title: Too many or too large pictures
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Your mod has more than 500 different pictures. Split it into smaller mods.
Your mod's pictures add up to more than 67 million pixels, or are too slow to check. Split it into smaller mods.

entries.meaning: Every picture in an upload is checked before it is accepted, so one upload may hold at most 500 different pictures, about 67 million pixels in all (16 textures of 2048 by 2048). The same file used many times counts once.
entries.fix: Split the mod into smaller mods, or make the large textures smaller.

entries.title: Not a GitHub repository and tag
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Write it as github.com/<owner>/<repo>@<tag>, for example github.com/you/tea-house@v1.2.0.
That is not a GitHub owner and repository name.

entries.meaning: Import from GitHub takes a public repository and one of its tags.
entries.fix: Write github.com/you/your-repo@v1.2.0, with a tag that exists on GitHub.

entries.title: That change to the version is not allowed now
where: the Mods tab

registry: A moderator took this version out of the list. Upload a fixed version, or ask the moderators to look again.
Another decision on this version came first. Reload and look again.

entries.meaning: A yank or unyank (or a moderator's decision) that the version's state does not allow: a version a moderator yanked is the moderator's to list again, and a decision someone else made first wins.
entries.fix: Reload the Mods tab. For a moderator's yank, read the reason, fix the mod and upload a new version.

entries.title: Update available
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

site: Update available

entries.meaning: A newer approved version of the mod is in the mod list.
entries.fix: Open Browse mods and install the update, then restart.

entries.title: No longer offered in the mod list
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

site: No longer offered in the mod list. It still works.

entries.meaning: The maker took this version out of the list (a yank). It still works and friend visits still match it, but new players cannot install it.
entries.fix: Nothing to do. If the maker shares a newer version, update to it.

entries.title: Mods are switched off for everyone
where: the Mods tab

registry: Mods are switched off for everyone for now while we fix a problem. Your mods are still installed and come back on their own.

entries.meaning: The site switched every mod off for a while (the kill switch). Games start without mods, and no mod can be downloaded until it is back on. Nothing is uninstalled.
entries.fix: Nothing to do: your mods come back on their own.

entries.title: A visit refused: world mods differ
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

site: Your world mods don't match. Visits need the same world mods (the ones visitors can see) in both towns (or none). Change them in Settings, Mods.
Kim's town runs Tea House 1.2.0, you don't. Visits need the same world mods (the ones visitors can see) in both towns. Change them in Settings, Mods.

entries.meaning: A friend visit starts only when both towns run the same world mods that count for visits, the same versions, in the same order, or both none. The message names what differs. Client mods never count. A world mod counts when it has "textures", "shops" or "items" content, or a command other than send_letter, give_item, set_flag, show_line and ask; one with only lines, letters, events or talk pools and those commands does not. When every one of your friend's world mods that counts is from Browse mods, you are offered their mods for that visit instead.
entries.fix: Both players open Settings, Mods, and make the world mods match: same mods, same versions (install from the same place or the same ZIP), same order. Or switch world mods off and restart. Makers: publish your world mod on Browse mods, so visitors can load it for a visit.

entries.title: A friend's mods could not be loaded for the visit
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

page: the download for bean.tea-house 1.2.0 does not match the friend's copy
the download for bean.tea-house 1.2.0 is a different mod
the friend's mods do not add up to their town's mod set
registry: Invalid mod list: the mod list does not match the mod set hash.
site: Couldn't load Kim's mods for this visit. Couldn't download Tea House: the registry answered 404.

entries.meaning: You agreed to visit with your friend's mods, and one of them could not be downloaded, or the download was not exactly the version your friend runs (checked by content hash). Nothing was kept or installed, and the visit was left.
entries.fix: Ask again later. If it keeps happening, the mod may have been taken down or updated: both players can install the same version from Browse mods.

entries.title: A City mod was refused
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

page: bean.lamps: a City mod may only hold textures and lines, not shops
bean.lamps: a City mod may not run scripts

entries.meaning: The City's own mod set (chosen by the site) may only change textures and lines. A mod with a shop, a script or commands is never loaded there.
entries.fix: Nothing for players to do: the site fixes its City set. Makers: a mod meant for The City holds only textures and messages.

entries.title: Nintendo or other franchise content
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds art, textures, models, music, sound or text taken from a Nintendo game or another game, film, show or brand, or redrawn copies of them. Mods here may only hold work you made yourself.
entries.fix: Replace every taken file with art you made yourself, then upload a new version. Redrawn copies of Nintendo art count as taken.

entries.title: Nintendo or franchise names or logos
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's name, id, description or pictures use Nintendo's names or logos, or another brand's, in a way that could make it look official. Give your mod its own name.
entries.fix: Rename the mod and its id, and remove logos from pictures. "AC" or "Animal Crossing" in a name can make it look official.

entries.title: Someone else's work
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds work made by someone else, such as another modder's files, without their permission. Share only what you made, or what you have written permission to share.
entries.fix: Remove the other person's files, or get their written permission and say so in the description.

entries.title: Removed after a copyright notice
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The owner of a copyright sent us a notice saying this mod copies their work, so it was removed. If you believe the notice is a mistake, the mod rules page says how to respond.
entries.fix: If you believe the notice is wrong, the mod rules page explains the counter-notice.

entries.title: Sexual content
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds sexual or sexually suggestive pictures or text. Players of every age use this site.
entries.fix: Remove it. Mods here are for players of every age.

entries.title: Hate or harassment
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod attacks or demeans people for who they are, or targets a real person to harass them.
entries.fix: Remove it.

entries.title: Personal information
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds someone's personal information, such as a real name with an address, a phone number, an email address or a photo of a real person.
entries.fix: Remove any real names with addresses, phone numbers, emails or photos of real people.

entries.title: Harmful script
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's script is made to break the game, slow it down on purpose, flood players with messages, or get around the limits mods run under.
entries.fix: Make the script do only what the description says, inside the limits. Do not try to get around the budget.

entries.title: Misleading
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's name, description or pictures do not match what it does, or it pretends to come from someone else.
entries.fix: Make the name, description and pictures match what the mod does.

entries.title: Does not work
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod does not load or does not do what it says. Fix it and upload it again as a new version.
entries.fix: Test it with the check tool and in the game (dev mode, the log panel), fix it, and upload a higher version.

entries.title: Spam or duplicate
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod repeats another upload, or is an advert or a placeholder rather than a mod.
entries.fix: Share each mod once, and only finished mods.

entries.title: Upload rights removed
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: Mods from this account were removed for copyright several times, so under the repeat-infringer policy on the mod rules page its mods are no longer shared.
entries.fix: See the mod rules page for how to appeal.

entries.title: Removed at your request
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: You asked for this version to be removed.
entries.fix: Nothing to do.

entries.title: Another rule
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod breaks another of the mod rules. The moderator's note says which.
entries.fix: Read the moderator's note: it says which rule.
